findings.title: Distinguish the contextual record identifier from a declaration keyword
findings.input: class C { void Run(object[] items) { foreach (var record in items) { } } }
findings.observed: The valid foreach variable named record yields an additional type finding with symbol in and symbol_kind record at offset 50.
findings.impact: The v2 projection treats this type as detected syntax and assigns high confidence when its bytes are pinned. A compiler-binding limitation does not qualify an incorrect lexical declaration.
findings.required_correction: Require a defensible declaration context/name for contextual record syntax and exclude reserved words used here as names; preserve actual record, record class and record struct declarations. Add the retained foreach reproduction and a projection assertion proving no false detected type is emitted.

findings.title: Stop named-delegate extraction before an anonymous delegate body
findings.input: class C { void Run() { System.Action a = delegate { Work(); }; } void Work() {} }
findings.observed: The parameterless anonymous delegate produces a delegate declaration named Work from its first body invocation at offset 41.
findings.impact: No named delegate is declared. The projected finding is nevertheless detected syntax with high confidence for pinned bytes, contrary to the helper contract that anonymous delegates are omitted.
findings.required_correction: Reject both anonymous-delegate forms before named-declaration scanning can cross into their body; retain actual named/generic delegates and the existing function-pointer exclusion. Add the retained parameterless anonymous-body reproduction and a projection assertion.

findings.title: Bound repeated declaration-prefix and generic rescans
findings.observed: Small adversarial generic/event-prefix inputs repeatedly scan shared token suffixes. Increasing repetitions 64 to 128 to 256 grows generic token indexing 8,832 to 34,048 to 133,632 and event-prefix indexing 4,671 to 17,535 to 67,839. Every call completes without a work-limit diagnostic.
findings.impact: Token/input/output limits do not bound aggregate scan work proportionately. Repeated suffix scans approach quadratic work before the existing 100,000-token cap; the member/event-subscription work limits do not cover these declaration helpers.
findings.required_correction: Apply one deterministic aggregate work bound to declaration rescans (or use equivalent one-pass spans), including generic and event/delegate prefix traversal. Reject excessive work with the established source-work-limit failure and no partial output claims. Add small deterministic regressions for both retained input families; do not add a large stress test or compiler dependency.
findings.instrumentation: A tuple subclass counts integer token reads; only tokenizer return is replaced with the identical token tuple in-process. Production bytes are unchanged.
